text:
Talia Benson: Kicking off cross-team coordination for Shadow Traffic ("Shadow Evals") workstream. Thread for ownership matrix + milestones + links so we’re not hunting across DMs.

Talia Benson: Links:
- PRD (eval metrics / customer-facing): <https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/PROD/Shadow+Traffic+Eval+Metrics+PRD|Shadow Traffic Eval Metrics PRD>
- Design spec (end-to-end): <https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ARCH/Shadow+Traffic+Tool+Architecture|Shadow Traffic Tool Architecture>
- Linear project: <https://linear.app/redwood/project/shadow-traffic-evals|Shadow Traffic Evals>
- Key eng tickets: ENG-2419 (shadow runner), ENG-2420 (RoutePolicy schema), ENG-2427 (telemetry pipeline), ENG-2431/2432 (Console)

Marissa Cole: Thanks Talia. Adding: the thing we need to keep repeating is “no impact to end-user response” + “no primary p99 regression.” If anything smells risky we default-off.

Dylan Brooks: :+1: Also please route any UI/terminology questions through Marissa + Kenji/Alicia early. We don’t want to ship an MVP that reads like an internal tool.

Talia Benson: Draft milestones (10-12 wks) from the plan:
1) Weeks 1-2: design + ADRs (mirroring approach, schema, retention/redaction, SLO budgets)
2) Weeks 3-6: MVP (shadow runner async path, queue, metrics emission, basic judge scoring integration)
3) Weeks 7-9: Console + guardrails (dashboards, comparisons, alerts, kill switch, cardinality controls)
4) Weeks 10-12: Beta + GA readiness (load tests, playbooks, docs, pricing/quotas, staged rollout)

Talia Benson: Can we confirm owners per workstream below? (If you’re not listed but you’re primary, shout.)
- Control plane / RoutePolicy schema + validation: Ethan / Benji
- Data plane shadow runner + isolation: Dylan (overall), Jada for rollouts integration points, Vikram/Emily as reviewers
- Telemetry schema/pipeline + datasets: Logan (lead), Mei/Nadia supporting
- Console backend/UI: Chloe + Dylan (backend), Kenji/Alicia for UX
- Evals/judge scoring guidance: Jonas / Selene
- SLOs/load tests/oncall readiness: Sean (lead) + Rafael
- Security retention/redaction/audit: Naomi (lead) + Marcus/Kevin

Ethan Park: Control plane side yes. ENG-2420 is ours. We’ll need final answers on: allowlist semantics + safe defaults. I’ll post a proposal doc this afternoon.

Benji Okafor: +1. Also we should decide if shadow targets are only “same route” or can reference a shared config. I’ve seen this explode complexity in other systems.

Jada Williams: Data plane: we can own the integration points from rollouts/A-B to the shadow runner (e.g., policy evaluation + request_id propagation). For the runner itself, I think Vikram/Emily are best placed but I can coordinate.

Chloe Martin: Console backend ok. FYI we’ll need stable metric/event schema from Logan’s team before we can lock query APIs. If schema changes weekly we’ll be whack-a-moling.

Logan Wright: Telemetry lead confirmed. Please everyone read this as “cardinality is the hill we die on.” If we put request-level tags into metrics, we will melt dashboards and/or bankrupt ourselves.

Allison Grant: +1 from obs standards side. Happy to review the naming/dimensions early. If we align now, SRE alerting is much easier later.

Sean Gallagher: SRE lead yes. Requirements from our side:
1) Shadow failures must not page as “customer-facing outage” unless they affect primary.
2) We need a global kill switch + per-route disable that does not require deploy.
3) Budgeting: hard caps (per region, per tier) with backpressure/drop counters.

Naomi Feldman: Security lead yes. Please treat “shadow payload” as potentially sensitive customer content. We need:
- redaction before any long-term persistence
- explicit retention controls (default conservative)
- access controls + audit logs for any raw payload samples

Jonas Weber: Evals: Selene + I can own judge scoring guidance + initial rubrics. Ask: we should scope judge gating to a minimal set first (format adherence + preference score), not “solve correctness.”

Selene Huang: Agree. Also, we should ship with “do not auto-roll back based solely on judge score” as default policy suggestion. Too many false positives early.

Marissa Cole: Re gating: the PRD language I’m using is “quality signals inform rollout guardrails,” but the default templates will be conservative. We can let customers dial it up once they calibrate.

Connor O'Brien: Release eng: once we have the guardrails/killswitch + dashboards, we can stage enablement by region. But I need a checklist with “must-have” before beta.

Talia Benson: Action items I’m capturing:
- Ethan/Benji: draft RoutePolicy shadow schema proposal + validation rules (incl safe defaults) (today)
- Logan/Allison: propose metric schema + allowed tags + aggregation strategy (this week)
- Sean: define SLO impact budget + initial alert thresholds (this week)
- Naomi: retention/redaction baseline + opt-out controls for beta (this week)
- Dylan/Jada: confirm shadow runner architecture ownership + dependencies (by EOW)
- Chloe/Dylan: outline Console API needs + dependency on telemetry tables (by EOW)
- Jonas/Selene: judge v1 rubric template + calibration plan + known failure modes (next week)

Linear: Created project update: "Kickoff actions captured in Slack" and linked issues ENG-2419, ENG-2420, ENG-2427, ENG-2431, ENG-2432.

Dylan Brooks: One more thing: we need a single “source of truth” for project state. Talia can we keep status in Linear + a weekly written update in #eng?

Talia Benson: Yes. Plan: weekly Monday update in #eng, and async standup notes in the Linear project update. Live sync 30 min on Thursdays for cross-team unblockers.

Chloe Martin: Quick Q: where are we putting the “ownership matrix” artifact? Confluence page? (So it doesn’t rot in Slack)

Talia Benson: I’ll add a Confluence page under the PRD section and link it back here. Will include owners, escalation, and “who approves what.”

Sean Gallagher: Can we define escalation now? If shadow is causing fleet pressure, SRE can flip the global kill switch without asking permission. Post-hoc comms in #incidents.

Marissa Cole: Works for me. We should document that explicitly so no one hesitates during beta.

Naomi Feldman: +1. Also document “security can force-disable retention/payload capture” if something is misconfigured.

Ethan Park: Re safe defaults: my take is shadow sampling default = 0% unless explicitly enabled per route + allowlist required for enterprise beta. No “accidental shadowing.”

Jada Williams: Agree. And we should ensure policy evaluation is deterministic and cached per route config version; we don’t want random behavior due to config race.

Logan Wright: Telemetry note: please do NOT emit per-request payload fields into metrics. Use events -> sampled logs (with redaction) -> aggregated tables. Metrics should be rollup-friendly.

Allison Grant: +1. If we need a dimension, we bucket it (e.g., token_count_bucket) and allowlist tags.

Jonas Weber: For judge: we can output per-run judge decision into events. The aggregated metric is win_rate / tie_rate with confidence intervals. We’ll need sample sizes in the dashboard or people will overreact.

Selene Huang: Yes please. “Win-rate dropped 3%” means nothing if N=40.

Connor O'Brien: For beta sequencing, we should target 1-2 accounts first with strict caps. If we go wide early, we’ll spend the entire time firefighting.

Talia Benson: Sounds aligned. I’ll post the Confluence owners/milestones page and tag everyone for review. Keep updates in this thread if anything changes / new dependencies surface.
